newsitem.title: UK: Mideast crude tanker fixing slows, rates steady.
newsitem.headline: Mideast crude tanker fixing slows, rates steady.

text.p: Crude tanker chartering in the all important Middle East Gulf slowed on Wednesday after strong activity earlier in the week.
Other lifting sectors saw freight rates sustain last done levels, shipping brokers said on Wednesday.
Middle Eastern rates remained steady on Tuesday, with VLCC rates to Japan estimated around the W65 region.
Tankers bound for the U.S and Europe were still assessed around W55, due primarily to good tonnage availability, London brokers said.
In the Mediterranean, chartering activity was fair and rates for 80,000 tonners remained around W100-103.

In the inter-UKC sector rates on 80,000 tonners were steady around W100, although up to W105 was done, with INPC seen taking the Prospect from Sture to Whitegate. Sun fixed a million barrel load to the U.S. atlantic coast at W87.5.

The Caribbean saw rates settle around last done levels, U.S. brokers said. They said 70,000 tonners travelling up the U.S. coast were steady around W130, although as low as W125 was done. West African rates strengthened marginally amid good chartering to the U.S. and Taiwan.
Brokers said rates for Suezmaxes to the U.S. were up slightly to W86.50 to W88, with Coastal taking the Corus WAF-USG at W88.75. A VLCC to the U.S. took W66.25 from Sohio.
